classification.difficultyReason: Apply the alternate segment theorem, then identify another angle standing on the same arc.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Circle with vertical diameter through O and tangent PT at its bottom endpoint T. Two circumference angles subtend the chord joining T to the right-hand circumference point. Source decorative hues are replaced by black; no shading is required.
spec.mathematics: The tangent–chord angle at T is 40 degrees. The top circumference angle x and lower-left circumference angle y stand on the same chord, on the side opposite the tangent–chord angle. All circumference points are coordinate-derived on the circle; the right-hand point is positioned to make the given tangent–chord angle exactly 40 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 40-degree angle and unknowns x and y appear. Supplied answers are omitted.

answer.worked:
$x=40^\circ$ (alternate segment theorem).

$y=x=40^\circ$ (angles at the circumference standing on the same arc are equal).
